geometry_hash_scope: UTF-8 JSON of the complete source geometry with sorted keys and compact separators; independent of file whitespace.
method: Rendered all source-ring coordinates with longitude/latitude axes, then visually compared the entire outline and its geographic extent with the NPS full-lake graticule map and regional park map. No centroid-only match, georeferenced raster overlay, exact shoreline overlap score or surveyed name-boundary claim.

region_checks.observation: The source’s broad western basin and short western tip align with the map’s Naknek basin and Lake Camp/outlet vicinity.
The source includes a northern lobe matching the guide’s locally labeled Johnny’s Lake basin. Local naming is retained as a scope qualification; separate official-lake status was not established.
The long east-west source arm and its southeastern notch match North Arm/Bay of Islands at generalized scale.
The source turns southeast at the Brooks Camp/moraine vicinity and extends east across Iliuk Arm.
The whole rendered target does not extend southwest into Lake Brooks or north across the land separation into Lake Grosvenor; those distinct neighboring basin shapes were checked on the two maps.

name_extent_assessment: The evidence supports generalized Naknek Lake identity for the mapped waterbody, with a local named-sub-basin qualification. It does not demonstrate that the polygon improperly combines independently scoped lakes, nor certify one official name for every coordinate.
precision_limits: Source is a generalized 1:10 million-scale polygon; local shoreline differences are expected.
The 2013 guide is not a current lake-level survey.
Complete source/rendered-coordinate verification belongs to the separate geometry-validation package.
No formal registry decision, legal name extent, Korean name or exact name-subdivision boundary was verified.
